objections.claim: The guard is specified as `regionsEmitCoverage(files)` added to `regions.js`, but the `files` it would naturally receive is `regionSources()`'s output, which `regions.js` builds as `[ENTRYPOINT, ...libFiles]` filtered to `.js` only. A `.ts` file that lacks its committed `.js` emit is by definition invisible to a `.js`-only file list: you cannot detect "a `.ts` without a sibling `.js`" by iterating `.js` names. As specified, the guard is vacuous — it can never fire — and the spec's own S6 ("`.ts` without its `.js` sibling → `faff regions check` exit 2") cannot pass against the letter of the design. The builder must silently deviate (enumerate `.ts` inside the guard, or widen `regionSources()`) to satisfy the acceptance test, which is exactly the kind of unspecified deviation this slice's whole point — a checkable, committed-emit contract — exists to prevent.
objections.evidence: spec §3 "Emit-coverage guard (folded from FAFF-1169) — Chosen" (`regionsEmitCoverage(files)` … "fails (exit 2) if any `.ts` under `bin/lib/` lacks a committed sibling `.js` emit"); `regions.js` `regionSources()` (`.js` filter) and `cmdRegions` `check` leg.
objections.predicted_consequence: S6 fails on first run against the spec-as-written implementation; the fix (a `regionSources()` widening or an in-guard directory listing) lands as an undocumented design change to a governance-adjacent lint that FAFF-1171's freshness gate then builds on.

objections.claim: The spec enumerates the package.json contents precisely (pinned devDeps, no `dependencies`, a `build` script) but omits the `type` field entirely. The entire runtime under it — `bin/faff`, `bin/commissaire`, and ~100 `bin/lib/*.js` modules — is CommonJS with no `package.json` above it today; introducing one without `"type": "commonjs"` leaves Node's module-type detection to default, and a builder who sets `"type": "module"` (a natural choice for a TypeScript project, and the direction S4c's run-`.ts`-directly lane nudges toward) makes every `.js` under `bin/` an ESM target: `require`/`module.exports` crash, the CLI dies on all four install paths. This is a one-word spec edit with a whole-artifact consequence, and the spec's own S4c (direct `.ts` execution, whose CJS/ESM outcome depends on exactly this field) makes the ambiguity load-bearing rather than incidental.
objections.evidence: spec §4 step 1 and §8 DONE ("`plugin/skills/faff/package.json` with pinned `typescript` … no `dependencies`, a `build` script"); spec S4c; `regions.js`/`commissaire.js` CommonJS shape; ADR-0132's adopter-path table (Node 20, extensionless CJS require).
objections.predicted_consequence: a build that sets `"type": "module"` passes `npm run build` and `tsc --noEmit` (S1/S4a) yet fails every S4b/S5 runtime scenario on all install paths — discovered late, after the toolchain is stood up.

objections.claim: The toolchain puts `node_modules` (typescript is tens of MB unpacked) at `plugin/skills/faff/` — the directory that is itself the shipped artifact (marketplace copy, in-checkout, governance action). The spec's clean-install smoke asserts "`node_modules` absent" for the copy, but names no mechanism that keeps a dev machine's installed `node_modules` out of the committed tree and out of the marketplace copy. The repo has a `gitignore-ensure` command and a `.gitignore` convention; the spec neither invokes it nor states any exclusion. Without one, the dependency-free-artifact pillar is enforced only by developer discipline — the exact class of unmechanised guarantee this codebase's own guards (region lint, emit-coverage) exist to replace.
objections.evidence: spec §3 toolchain ("`package.json` and `tsconfig.json` live at `plugin/skills/faff/`"), §8 DONE ("Clean-install smoke … `node_modules` absent"); the "shipped artifact stays dependency-free" principle.
objections.predicted_consequence: a dev runs `npm install`, commits the tree, and the plugin ships with a multi-MB `node_modules` (or the marketplace copy picks it up), silently voiding the dependency-free claim the spec's first principle asserts.

objections.claim: The checker's three properties catch only *explicit* assertion forms (`as`/`<T>`/`!`/`satisfies`), *declared* `any` return types on named readers, and the one `producer-auth` binding. But `commissaire.ts` still requires six-plus unconverted JS siblings (`events.js`, `effects.js`, `shared-infra.js`, `budget.js`, `sentry.js`, `bundle-seal-core.js`) whose exports infer as `any`/loose types under `allowJs`. A value returned by e.g. `readLedger(runDir)` (consumed by `cmdAdmitRequired` for `ledger.level`) or `appendRecordsUnderLock`/`computeEscapes` can be consumed directly with no cast, no declared-`any` reader, and no typed require — implicit `any` propagation, which `noImplicitAny` does not flag (the any originates in the JS sibling's inference, not an annotation) and the checker does not enumerate. The spec's own principle ("every value arriving from outside a module … is pinned by a runtime validator") is thus unenforceable by the tooling the spec ships for every sibling except `producer-auth`: nothing fires when a future edit consumes an any-typed ledger field without routing it through `parseGovernedRecord`/`parseAdmissionRecord`.
objections.evidence: §3 "Boundary-contract check — Chosen" (properties 1–3 as enumerated); §3 "Validated input boundaries" lists "on-disk JSON/JSONL … subprocess stdout" and "cross-module `ProducerId`/`ContractRevisionId` call sites" — the typed-require enforcement (property 3) names only the `producer-auth` binding, leaving the other JS-sibling edges uninstrumented.
objections.predicted_consequence: a ledger-derived, attacker-influencable field (record fields read off `declared-effects.jsonl` / `run-ledger.json`) can be consumed in `commissaire.ts` with no runtime validation and no tool fires — the cast-prohibition control is silently narrower than the boundary set the spec declares, and the gap grows with every sibling that stays JS.

objections.claim: The DONE item "producer-auth.ts runs directly on Node 22.18+" and scenario S4c's "(startup probe)" name no command and no expected observable. `producer-auth.ts` is a library — executing it as a script defines functions and exits 0 while proving nothing; requiring it under type-stripping proves the emit-free lane but the spec never says which, nor what the probe must observe (exit 0? a called function's return?).
objections.evidence: S4c "Leaf runs un-built"; DONE "producer-auth.ts runs directly on Node 22.18+"; DONE "startup recorded for source and emit".
objections.predicted_consequence: two conformant builds can satisfy this DONE item with different probes (bare `node producer-auth.ts` vs a require-and-call harness), so the "runs un-built" claim is not decidable to a single standard.
